## Why

I chose a set of balancing scales, featuring a mitre in one pan and a heavy, standardized rule in the other, as the single recognizable subject. This form encapsulates *Cum illud semper*'s core demand for justice and order in the selection of rectors, directly visualizing the competitive examination (the rule) as the objective counterweight to worthiness for office (the mitre). The subject is immediately legible and concrete, unlike an abstract representation of fairness; it avoids the complexity of a tableau or diorama by presenting a unified, ancient symbol of standardized judgment and pastoral authority.

## Why

I have selected a set of balancing scales, a universally recognized symbol of justice and examination, to embody the core message of *Cum illud semper*. To ground the concept specifically within the context of Benedict XIV's instructions, I have placed a clerical mitre on one pan, representing the pastoral office, and a standardized metal gauge and weights on the other, representing the strict, standardized competitive examinations prescribed by the Pope. This single, unified subject perfectly captures the encyclical's drive to restore integrity to the appointment system, weighing the worthiness of candidates against an objective, measurable standard to eliminate abuse. Abstraction was avoided to ensure the connection between pastoral care and the necessity for rigorous examination remains concrete and immediately legible.
